interest: This document is historically valuable as a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) compiled at the end of World War II (October 1945), summarizing recurring American concerns during the 1930s over potential Japanese naval and coaling installations in Mexico. It demonstrates the enduring sensitivity of the U.S. government to foreign naval presence near its southern border—especially echoing the Magdalena Bay scare of 1912 and the Lodge Corollary. Furthermore, it illustrates diplomatic caution in intelligence gathering, recording the Department's explicit refusal to participate in an observation cruise arranged by a private Mexicali ship owner, while providing key cross-references to related military and bilateral decimal files (894.20212 and 712.94).
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing documents filed under decimal classification 894.34512 concerning Japanese naval and coaling stations in Mexico. The docket sheet indexes correspondence and reports spanning from 1931 to 1938 regarding suspected Japanese maritime and naval ambitions in Lower California and the Gulf of California. Specific entries record an inquiry by historian Thomas A. Bailey regarding reported Japanese efforts to acquire land at Magdalena Bay, claims by Harry Downes regarding a Japanese naval base in Lower California, and several despatches from American Consul Horatio Mooers at Mexicali reporting local rumors of a base, general Japanese activities, and a proposed coastal observation cruise that the Department advised against accepting.

subfiles.about: A State Department docket sheet indexing correspondence and reports from 1931 to 1938 regarding alleged Japanese coaling and naval stations in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: This Form DS-46 List of Papers, compiled on October 12, 1945, serves as the registry sheet for decimal file 894.34512, tracking documents related to Japanese coaling stations and naval ambitions in Mexico. It indexes six separate communications from 1931 to 1938, including inquiries by Thomas A. Bailey on Magdalena Bay, reports from Harry Downes on Lower California, and despatches from Consul Horatio Mooers in Mexicali regarding suspected naval bases in the Gulf of California. The sheet also records a State Department instruction discouraging consular participation in a private coastal reconnaissance cruise, as well as cross-references to files 894.20212 and 712.94.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Coaling Stations of Japan in Mexico
